control_calibration.title: Do the controls read zero?
control_calibration.question: Genes known to do nothing must calibrate to a standard normal. Anything else means the null is wrong.

control_qq.title: Where exactly do the controls depart from normal?
control_qq.question: On a Q-Q plot a correct null is the diagonal. An offset is bias, a slope is the wrong spread, and curvature at the ends is tail misfit.

null_curve.title: What the score reads when nothing is happening
null_curve.question: The null's mean and spread as a function of observation count. The slope is the bias a raw ranking would inherit.

null_ridgeline.title: The null is not a mean and a spread - it has a shape
null_ridgeline.question: The distribution of the statistic under no effect, at each observation count. A top-k operator produces a skewed null, which a band hides.

funnel.title: Score against the precision behind it
funnel.question: A raw score is not comparable across counts. The funnel says how far from the null a score has to be, given how well it was measured.

rank_shift.title: What calibration did to the ranking
rank_shift.question: The library's only claim is about ordering, so this is the figure that tests it. Controls should fall; the confound should be visible.

count_distribution.title: How much does the observation count actually vary?
count_distribution.question: The correction reorders a ranking only when counts differ. So the first thing to plot about any screen is whether they do.
